extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students and policymakers interested in stakeholder consultations and public policymaking (particularly EU/executive bureaucracies)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and research-focused criteria for assessing how stakeholder consultations (public consultations, surveys, hearings, expert groups, etc.) affect the inputs, processes and outcomes of executive policymaking across policy areas and political systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic goods (legitimacy and participatory benefits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether consultations 'deliver the promised “democratic goods”' — i.e., whether participation via consultations produces legitimate, democratically valuable outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames a central debate around whether consultations actually increase legitimacy and democratic quality or are merely performative. Use measures of perceived legitimacy, democratic endorsement, and whether consultations tangibly connect citizens/organizations to decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amelioration of biases in interest representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which consultations 'ameliorate existing biases in interest representation' by broadening whose views are heard and used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess representational balance across types of actors (citizens vs organized interests, resource-rich vs resource-poor groups). The project notes intense scholarly debate on whether consultations reduce or reproduce representation biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and inclusiveness of bureaucratic policymaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether consultations increase the openness and inclusiveness of executive policymaking processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalise through metrics such as number and diversity of participants, barriers to access, transparency of procedures, and whether marginalized actors can meaningfully participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement of evidence-based decision-making / informational quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether consultations improve evidence-based policymaking by increasing the informational quality of inputs received by policymakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project foregrounds 'informational quality' as a key outcome; evaluate content quality of submissions (relevance, specificity, expertise, novel information) rather than just quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive influence versus symbolic 'window-dressing'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether consultations are meaningful inputs to decision-making or are 'a “mere plebiscite”, a “window-dressing” exercise organised to legitimise bureaucratic decision-making and policy choices.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish symbolic/signalling uses (legitimising rhetoric) from substantive policymaker responsiveness. Anti-patterns include consultations conducted primarily to claim legitimacy without changing choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative cost and resource burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs and administrative manpower required to organise and run consultations, and whether those costs are justified by benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider resource intensity (staff time, processing costs) and cost-effectiveness; the page notes consultations 'are costly and require substantial administrative and manpower resource'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information overload and decision-making efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which consultations create information overload for policymakers and potentially reduce decision-making efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure processing capacity, timeliness of decisions, filtering mechanisms used, and whether high volumes of input degrade policy quality or slow processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality of policy input
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which consultations increase the plurality (variety, diversity) of policy inputs policymakers receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether consultations bring in multiple perspectives, alternative proposals, and a spread of policy options rather than narrow, homogenous input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of public comments / textual informational content
rubrics_metrics.description: The information quality of public comments (e.g., relevance, argumentation, evidence) — referenced in the project's publication on 'information quality of public comments'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational measures can include textual-content analyses (text-as-data), argument strength, factual content, and contribution to policy-relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency of the policy process
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether consultations affect the efficiency of the policymaking process (speed, coherence, administrative burden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to information overload and cost; evaluate trade-offs between thorough stakeholder input and timely policy formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and legitimacy of policy outputs and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether consultation participation improves the substantive quality of policy outputs and the legitimacy of resulting policies and outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes to assess include policy effectiveness, implementation success, legal robustness, and perceived legitimacy by stakeholders and publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder support for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether public participation via consultations 'fosters stakeholder support for policy proposals' and eases implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure changes in stakeholder endorsement, compliance intent, and practical support for policies following engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policymaker responsiveness and use of stakeholder input
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which executive bureaucracies (ministries, agencies, Commission) incorporate stakeholder input into the design and formulation of policy proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate instances of substantive changes attributable to consultation input, citation of submissions in drafts, and documented responsiveness. The page emphasises consultations as a 'direct communication link' providing feedback on feasibility, legitimacy and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and conditional factors shaping effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Under what conditions (policy area, system of governance, institutional design) do consultations improve processes and outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project asks 'To what extent and under what conditions...' — so criteria should include contextual moderators like governance system, policy sector, political salience, institutional incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation design features and trade-offs (optimal design)
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes an optimal stakeholder consultation design that 'simultaneously enhances public legitimacy, accountability and representativeness of bureaucratic policymaking, as well as its policy efficiency and effectiveness'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design dimensions to evaluate include selection/targeting of participants, timing, format (public consultation, survey, hearing, workshop, expert group), framing of questions, feedback loops, and mechanisms to process/filter input. The page highlights the need to reconcile multiple goals (legitimacy, accountability, representativeness, efficiency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode/type of consultation (methodological modality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that a 'variety of consultation practices (i.e. public consultations, online surveys, public hearings, stakeholder workshops, expert groups, advisory committees)' are used and that mode may affect outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat consultation modality as a metric: different formats likely yield different participation profiles, information quality, and influence pathways; evaluate format-specific strengths and weaknesses.
